Retrieval practice and memory

Retrieval practice strengthens memory by asking learners to recall ideas before rereading them. One practical approach is to close the book and write down the main points from memory. The learner then checks the original material to identify missing details and correct mistakes.

Spacing these attempts across several days gives learners repeated opportunities to recall. A short review can begin with one concrete question about the previous reading. The answer should be compared with the original passage before moving to another topic.
